page: Microsoft Azure D160as_v7 is a high-density general-purpose virtual machine based on the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor architecture, managed under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system provides 160 dedicated vCPUs derived from 80 physical cores with two threads per core, running at clock frequencies up to 4.5 GHz. Memory configuration totals 640.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Advanced instruction extensions are supported on the chip, including AVX-512 vector operations, AVX-VNNI for neural network inferencing, and hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions such as AES and SHA_NI.

The D160as_v7 includes no local instance storage and provides no hardware GPU accelerators, requiring all operational persistence to rely on network-attached Premium Storage. Benchmark results position the server in the top tier across multi-threaded computational workloads, registering 289,369.62 in stress-ng multi-core testing and 29,137.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks reach 464.03 GB/sec for reads and 209.97 GB/sec for writes. The platform also demonstrates high throughput in memory-bound caching scenarios, achieving 200.12 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations, alongside 114.9 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the instance aggregates massive compute and memory capacity into a single virtual machine boundary, reducing orchestration overhead for monolithic or large multi-threaded runtimes. The lack of bundled local NVMe storage means storage throughput depends entirely on attached block volume tiers, which represents an architectural consideration for I/O-intensive workloads. Given its balanced resource distribution and high multi-core throughput, the D160as_v7 is suited for enterprise software compilation, large in-memory databases, dense web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D160as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 160 dedicated vCPUs across 80 physical cores at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz, paired with 640 GB of RAM to sustain a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation. Architectural capabilities include hardware support for AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and advanced cryptographic extensions. The virtual machine does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, necessitating remote network-attached disks for persistent persistence. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the D160as_v7 achieves top-tier results in multi-core compute, uncached memory bandwidth, and in-memory key-value throughput, recording over 200 million Redis operations per second. This instance offers strong resource density and compute efficiency for highly parallelized enterprise workloads, large software builds, heavy in-memory data processing, web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
